instructions.name: depth-before-size
instructions.title: Deeper, not bigger
instructions.text: Before you write the plan, answer in a few lines: what would an expert in this field do here that the brief doesn't ask for; what is the rawest material to start from (the real failing output, the files, the logs) instead of a summary; which methods and tools would they use; and what, other than you or the user, shows the result is right (name the artifact). Put the answers at the top of the plan as choices the user can take or leave.

instructions.name: fast-checks
instructions.title: Fastest check that proves it
instructions.text: Give this state the fastest check that proves its work: one test file, a type check or a build. Leave whole suites for the final checks.

instructions.name: failure-list
instructions.title: Failure list first
instructions.text: Before writing logic, write down how it can fail and test each item, with the tests written before the code. Tests written after the code to raise coverage end up restating it.

instructions.name: fails-first
instructions.title: Check fails before the work
instructions.text: Sentinel runs the state's check once before any edit. If it already passes, Claude is told the check proves nothing yet and tightens it.

instructions.name: break-it-once
instructions.title: A test must be able to fail
instructions.text: Break the code each new test targets once and watch the test fail, then put the code back. Report any test you couldn't make fail.

instructions.name: fails-without-change
instructions.title: Check fails without the change
instructions.text: Before a state closes, Sentinel reruns its check in a scratch copy that has the state's test changes but not its code changes. If the check still passes there, the advance is refused until the check is tightened or Claude records why with decide. If it fails, Sentinel runs it once more with the code changes in, to tell a real failure from a copy that can't run the check.

instructions.name: prove-end-to-end
instructions.title: Prove it end to end
instructions.text: A feature that crosses parts ends with an end-to-end run that leaves an artifact anyone can rerun and a script can check: the command and its saved output, a rendered image, a log.

instructions.name: measure-before-delete
instructions.title: Delete tests only after measuring
instructions.needs: A mutation-testing tool, such as Stryker or go-mutesting.
instructions.text: Delete a test only after a mutation run shows it catches nothing the others don't. Never by reading alone.

instructions.name: sources-first
instructions.title: Plan from the raw sources
instructions.text: Plan from the raw sources (the TRD, the design frames, the sprint sheet), not summaries of them. Where they disagree, the TRD decides behaviour and data, the design decides screens, and the sprint sheet decides scope and order. List each conflict at the top of the plan, and ask before departing from the TRD on anything structural.

instructions.name: api-errors
instructions.description: Errors a person can act on
instructions.text: Every error the API returns carries a code and one sentence that says what to do next.

flowSaid.text: The weight is thorough for this project. The built-ins follow it; your own items keep their switches.

states.label: Limit each key
states.title: Hold each key to 60 a minute
states.problem: One client can flood the API and slow it for everyone.
states.approach: A token bucket per API key, answering 429 with a Retry-After header.

states.label: Load test
states.title: Show the limit holds under load
states.problem: A limiter can pass its tests and still leak under real traffic.
states.approach: Send 5,000 requests a minute from 20 keys and count what gets through.

states.label: Document the limits
states.title: Tell clients the limits
states.problem: Clients need to know the limit and what a 429 means.
states.approach: Add a section with the headers and an example.
